instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me
cards.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded at Friday. I'll record that you've accepted me as project lead; the minutes need a clear decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only agreed to the meeting date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The date I set. That's acceptance of my timetable. Please don't record the same decision twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll attend, but I'm voting against your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll list you as my finance watchdog. Send your objections before Friday so I can put your contribution under my opening report.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. Give me control of the keys, please; access has to be consistent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's a key, but the cleaners lock the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then their checklist is wrong. Send it to me for approval; equipment stays accessible after cleaning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then send me the manager's instructions before they go out. I'll correct those first; the contractor can work from my approved version.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your deliveries interrupt meetings. Send the van schedule for my approval; arrivals need proper coordination.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You book the rooms. I'll send you our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Times without routes aren't a schedule I can verify. Send both, please, and wait for my approval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council keeps closing the access road. We can't schedule around that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give their roads team my booking calendar. Ask them to submit closures before confirming them. Proposed dates, please, not another notice after the barriers go up.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come paint Dad's kitchen with me. I'll handle the cutting-in; since he died, I barely see you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay someone. I can't paint over his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We don't paint the marks. Low-tack tape around them, then brush away from the edge. Come hold the tape straight for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put the dust sheet down before you sit. No paint tins in the way. Just come, please; I want you there, not a replacement painter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, come to my sculpture opening. I need someone I trust beside the big piece; I'll show you where to stand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't need to explain it. Help me unpack it: support the base, never the thin arm. I'd like you there for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your mother will be there. We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come at five, before Mum arrives. We'll unpack it together, then I'll take you round. Let me show you what I've made before the room fills up.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Dry your hands and sit down, please. We're still barely speaking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to clean up. I've done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Correct. That's the kitchen finished. Don't sign us off with it; tell me whether you still want to come back tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only got ten minutes before I need to leave for the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me five. One question, one answer; we can manage that properly. Please sit where I can hear you, not halfway through the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi yet. The bags are ready; we are not. Sit down, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologised for telling my sister about your debt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You named what you did. We haven't agreed what stays between us now. Let's finish that before we leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for dinner. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her 'We're running late.' Nothing about my debt. Then sit here and promise me tonight stays between us.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised for missing my concert. Now tell me what you think it cost me to keep looking at your empty seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the cause of your absence. I'm asking about its effect on me. Keep those separate, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then look at the moment before the encore, when I turn toward the door. Start there. I was still expecting you; tell me you understand that part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me what six weeks without an answer did to me. Not what happened to the phone; what happened to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The phone broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the equipment failure. I didn't know about it. Please answer the question about the person waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You thought I'd stopped caring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. And every morning I rewrote my message to make it easier to answer. Include that, please: I thought I was the difficult part.
